title: Agricultural Policy
source_note: Grounded in standard Nigerian agricultural policy history and analysis as taught in NUC-aligned agricultural economics/extension curricula, covering colonial-era policy through recent national agricultural transformation programmes.

questions.question: In general terms, what is 'agricultural policy'?
options: A set of deliberate government decisions and actions aimed at achieving specific objectives in the agricultural sector
A private company's internal farm safety manual
A university course outline for crop science
A single law that only regulates fertilizer prices
questions.correct_answer: A set of deliberate government decisions and actions aimed at achieving specific objectives in the agricultural sector
questions.explanation: Agricultural policy is the framework of government goals, principles, and actions designed to guide the development of agriculture.

questions.question: During the colonial era, Nigerian agricultural policy was primarily oriented toward what objective?
options: Promoting the production of export cash crops such as cocoa, groundnut, and palm produce for the colonial economy
Achieving full food self-sufficiency for local consumption
Distributing free land to all rural farmers
Establishing state-owned mechanized food crop farms nationwide
questions.correct_answer: Promoting the production of export cash crops such as cocoa, groundnut, and palm produce for the colonial economy
questions.explanation: Colonial agricultural policy emphasized cash crop exports to supply raw materials to the metropole, often at the expense of food crop development.

questions.question: Commodity marketing boards established in colonial and early post-independence Nigeria were primarily responsible for what?
options: Controlling the purchase, pricing, and export of major cash crops from farmers
Providing free university education to farmers' children
Building rural hospitals
Regulating the national currency
questions.correct_answer: Controlling the purchase, pricing, and export of major cash crops from farmers
questions.explanation: Marketing boards had monopoly power to buy export crops from farmers at fixed prices and handle their sale on international markets, often taxing farmers heavily through price differentials.

questions.question: The 'Operation Feed the Nation' (OFN) programme launched in 1976 in Nigeria was aimed primarily at what?
options: Mobilizing citizens, including non-farmers, to boost food production and achieve national food self-sufficiency
Establishing marketing boards for cash crops
Creating the Central Bank of Nigeria
Privatizing all government farms
questions.correct_answer: Mobilizing citizens, including non-farmers, to boost food production and achieve national food self-sufficiency
questions.explanation: OFN was a national mobilization campaign encouraging all Nigerians, including urban dwellers, to engage in food production to address rising food imports.

questions.question: The 'Green Revolution' programme of 1980 in Nigeria succeeded Operation Feed the Nation with what primary emphasis?
options: A more technically driven approach using improved inputs, credit, and mechanization to raise agricultural output
Banning the use of fertilizer nationwide
Shutting down all agricultural research institutes
Focusing solely on livestock export taxation
questions.correct_answer: A more technically driven approach using improved inputs, credit, and mechanization to raise agricultural output
questions.explanation: The Green Revolution programme aimed to modernize agriculture through improved seeds, fertilizer, irrigation, and credit access.

questions.question: The Structural Adjustment Programme (SAP) introduced in Nigeria in 1986 affected agricultural policy mainly by doing what?
options: Deregulating markets, removing subsidies, and abolishing commodity marketing boards to allow market-driven prices
Nationalizing all farms under direct federal control
Introducing free healthcare for farmers
Banning the export of all agricultural commodities
questions.correct_answer: Deregulating markets, removing subsidies, and abolishing commodity marketing boards to allow market-driven prices
questions.explanation: SAP pursued market liberalization, removing input subsidies and dismantling commodity boards in favor of private sector-led pricing and trade.

questions.question: The Land Use Act of 1978 in Nigeria primarily achieved which reform?
options: Vesting ownership of all land in each state in the Governor, held in trust for the people
Privatizing all agricultural land to foreign investors
Abolishing customary land tenure entirely with no compensation provisions
Transferring all farmland ownership to the federal government exclusively
questions.correct_answer: Vesting ownership of all land in each state in the Governor, held in trust for the people
questions.explanation: The Land Use Act nationalized land administration by vesting radical title in state Governors, who hold land in trust and grant rights of occupancy.

questions.question: Which of the following is a common objective found in most national agricultural policy documents, including Nigeria's National Agricultural Policy?
options: Attainment of food security and self-sufficiency
Elimination of all agricultural exports
Complete abolition of private land ownership
Reduction of national food production
questions.correct_answer: Attainment of food security and self-sufficiency
questions.explanation: Food security is a near-universal objective across Nigeria's successive agricultural policy frameworks.

questions.question: The Agricultural Transformation Agenda (ATA), launched around 2011, is best characterized by which approach?
options: Treating agriculture as a business (agribusiness) with value chain development and direct input delivery via e-wallet to farmers
Returning to the marketing board system of the 1950s
Banning all fertilizer subsidies
Focusing exclusively on livestock veterinary services
questions.correct_answer: Treating agriculture as a business (agribusiness) with value chain development and direct input delivery via e-wallet to farmers
questions.explanation: ATA repositioned agriculture as a business, introducing the Growth Enhancement Support Scheme (GESS) e-wallet system for direct input delivery, and emphasized value chains.

questions.question: The Agriculture Promotion Policy (APP), also known as the 'Green Alternative' (2016-2020), primarily focused on which two pillars?
options: Achieving food security and generating economic growth/import substitution through agriculture
Nationalizing all farms and abolishing private investment
Promoting only livestock production nationwide
Reducing agricultural exports to zero
questions.correct_answer: Achieving food security and generating economic growth/import substitution through agriculture
questions.explanation: The APP's Green Alternative built on ATA, emphasizing food security and using agriculture to diversify the economy away from oil.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of an input subsidy policy in agriculture?
options: To reduce the cost of farm inputs like fertilizer and seeds to farmers, encouraging greater uptake and productivity
To increase the retail price of farm produce for consumers
To discourage farmers from using improved seeds
To transfer land ownership from farmers to government
questions.correct_answer: To reduce the cost of farm inputs like fertilizer and seeds to farmers, encouraging greater uptake and productivity
questions.explanation: Input subsidies lower the effective price farmers pay for inputs, aiming to boost adoption of yield-enhancing technologies.

questions.question: A price support policy in agriculture typically involves the government doing what?
options: Setting a guaranteed minimum price for a commodity to protect farmers from price crashes
Fixing the maximum wage of farm laborers
Banning the sale of a commodity entirely
Removing all taxes on imported food
questions.correct_answer: Setting a guaranteed minimum price for a commodity to protect farmers from price crashes
questions.explanation: Price support (or floor price) policies guarantee farmers a minimum price, insulating them from market price volatility.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a 'tariff' as a trade policy instrument in agriculture?
options: A tax imposed on imported agricultural goods to make them more expensive relative to domestic produce
A subsidy paid directly to farmers for exporting crops
A ban on all forms of agricultural trade
A grant given to consumers to buy imported food
questions.correct_answer: A tax imposed on imported agricultural goods to make them more expensive relative to domestic produce
questions.explanation: Tariffs raise the price of imports, protecting domestic producers from cheaper foreign competition.

questions.question: An import quota, as an agricultural trade policy tool, works by doing what?
options: Limiting the physical quantity of a commodity that can be imported within a given period
Fixing the domestic retail price of the commodity
Eliminating all restrictions on imports
Subsidizing foreign farmers directly
questions.correct_answer: Limiting the physical quantity of a commodity that can be imported within a given period
questions.explanation: A quota is a direct quantitative restriction on imports, unlike a tariff which works through price.

questions.question: The Anchor Borrowers' Programme, introduced by the Central Bank of Nigeria, is primarily designed to do what?
options: Provide farm input credit to smallholder farmers linked to agro-processors ('anchors') who purchase their produce
Provide free land titles to urban dwellers
Replace the Land Use Act entirely
Eliminate all agricultural export taxes
questions.correct_answer: Provide farm input credit to smallholder farmers linked to agro-processors ('anchors') who purchase their produce
questions.explanation: The ABP links smallholder farmers to processors, providing inputs on credit that is repaid in kind or cash from produce sales, strengthening value chains.

questions.question: The Agricultural Credit Guarantee Scheme Fund (ACGSF) in Nigeria primarily serves what function?
options: Guaranteeing a portion of loans given by commercial banks to farmers to reduce lending risk
Printing new currency for agricultural transactions
Directly employing all extension agents in Nigeria
Setting the exchange rate for agricultural exports
questions.correct_answer: Guaranteeing a portion of loans given by commercial banks to farmers to reduce lending risk
questions.explanation: ACGSF shares default risk with banks, encouraging them to lend more freely to the agricultural sector.

questions.question: Which international organization is primarily concerned with global efforts to eliminate hunger and improve nutrition and food security?
options: Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO)
World Health Organization (WHO)
International Monetary Fund (IMF)
World Trade Organization (WTO)
questions.correct_answer: Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO)
questions.explanation: The FAO is the UN specialized agency leading international efforts to defeat hunger and improve agriculture, forestry, and fisheries.

questions.question: The World Bank's involvement in Nigerian agricultural policy has historically included what kind of support?
options: Financing and technical support for programmes such as the Agricultural Development Programmes (ADPs)
Direct control of Nigeria's central bank
Setting Nigeria's national elections calendar
Managing Nigeria's judiciary
questions.correct_answer: Financing and technical support for programmes such as the Agricultural Development Programmes (ADPs)
questions.explanation: The World Bank provided major funding and technical design support for Nigeria's ADP system starting in the 1970s.

questions.question: What is the primary role of the International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD)?
options: Financing projects that reduce rural poverty and improve food security in developing countries
Regulating global stock exchanges
Enforcing international trade sanctions
Managing global weather forecasting
questions.correct_answer: Financing projects that reduce rural poverty and improve food security in developing countries
questions.explanation: IFAD is a UN specialized agency dedicated to financing agricultural development and rural poverty reduction.

questions.question: In policy analysis, 'policy formulation' refers to which stage of the policy process?
options: The stage where alternative solutions to an identified problem are developed and a course of action is chosen
The stage where a policy is repealed
The stage of collecting taxes
The final stage after a policy has already been evaluated
questions.correct_answer: The stage where alternative solutions to an identified problem are developed and a course of action is chosen
questions.explanation: Policy formulation follows problem identification and involves designing and selecting among alternative courses of action.

questions.question: Which stage of the policy cycle involves translating an adopted policy into actual programmes and actions on the ground?
options: Policy implementation
Agenda setting
Problem identification
Policy termination
questions.correct_answer: Policy implementation
questions.explanation: Implementation is the stage where formulated policy is put into practice through specific programmes, budgets, and institutional actions.

questions.question: Why is policy evaluation an important stage in agricultural policy management?
options: It determines whether policy objectives were achieved and informs future policy adjustments
It is only done to punish non-compliant farmers
It eliminates the need for policy implementation
It replaces the role of the legislature
questions.correct_answer: It determines whether policy objectives were achieved and informs future policy adjustments
questions.explanation: Evaluation assesses policy outcomes against intended objectives, providing feedback for revising or redesigning future policy.

questions.question: A cooperative society, as recognized in Nigerian agricultural policy, is best described as which of the following?
options: A voluntary association of farmers who pool resources for mutual economic benefit, such as bulk input purchase or marketing
A government agency that fixes farm produce prices
A private multinational agribusiness corporation
A court that settles land disputes
questions.correct_answer: A voluntary association of farmers who pool resources for mutual economic benefit, such as bulk input purchase or marketing
questions.explanation: Agricultural cooperatives allow farmers to combine resources for purchasing inputs, accessing credit, and marketing produce more efficiently than acting alone.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes 'land tenure' in the context of agricultural policy?
options: The system of rules defining how land is owned, held, and transferred within a society
The chemical composition of farm soil
The annual rainfall pattern of a region
The list of crops grown in a particular season
questions.correct_answer: The system of rules defining how land is owned, held, and transferred within a society
questions.explanation: Land tenure encompasses the institutional arrangements governing rights to hold, use, and transfer land, a key subject of agricultural land policy.

questions.question: One major criticism of the Land Use Act of 1978 relates to which of the following?
options: Bureaucratic delays and difficulty in obtaining certificates of occupancy, which can discourage agricultural investment
It made all land privately owned with no government role
It abolished the office of the state Governor
It made land acquisition entirely free of any administrative process
questions.correct_answer: Bureaucratic delays and difficulty in obtaining certificates of occupancy, which can discourage agricultural investment
questions.explanation: Critics note that the Act's administrative processes for obtaining rights of occupancy are often slow and costly, hindering land access for agricultural investment.

questions.question: What is the main goal of a national food security policy?
options: Ensuring all citizens have physical and economic access to sufficient, safe, and nutritious food at all times
Maximizing the export of staple food crops regardless of domestic shortages
Reducing the number of registered farmers
Eliminating all agricultural imports permanently
questions.correct_answer: Ensuring all citizens have physical and economic access to sufficient, safe, and nutritious food at all times
questions.explanation: Food security policy targets availability, access, utilization, and stability of food supply for the whole population.

questions.question: Which policy instrument directly channels government funds to reduce farmers' production costs, distinct from a market price intervention?
options: Subsidy
Tariff
Import ban
Export tax
questions.correct_answer: Subsidy
questions.explanation: A subsidy is a direct financial transfer that lowers the cost of production or inputs for producers.

questions.question: Why might a government impose an export tax on an agricultural commodity?
options: To discourage excessive export and ensure sufficient domestic supply, or to raise government revenue
To increase farmers' export earnings without limit
To eliminate all foreign demand for the crop
To make the commodity free for foreign buyers
questions.correct_answer: To discourage excessive export and ensure sufficient domestic supply, or to raise government revenue
questions.explanation: Export taxes can be used to retain a commodity domestically for food security or processing, while also generating government revenue.

questions.question: What was a key weakness of Nigeria's commodity marketing boards that contributed to their eventual abolition under SAP?
options: They often paid farmers prices well below world market prices, discouraging production
They paid farmers prices far above world market prices
They had no role in setting prices at all
They were run entirely by farmers themselves with no government involvement
questions.correct_answer: They often paid farmers prices well below world market prices, discouraging production
questions.explanation: Marketing boards frequently retained large price margins as revenue, effectively taxing farmers and discouraging cash crop production over time.

questions.question: Which of the following is a key policy instrument used specifically for stabilizing farm produce prices through government buying and storage?
options: Strategic grain reserve / buffer stock scheme
Export subsidy for finished manufactured goods
Import ban on machinery
Corporate income tax exemption for banks
questions.correct_answer: Strategic grain reserve / buffer stock scheme
questions.explanation: A buffer stock or strategic reserve scheme buys grain in surplus periods and releases it in scarcity, stabilizing prices and supply.

questions.question: In agricultural policy analysis, what does 'policy instrument' mean?
options: A specific tool or mechanism (e.g., subsidy, tariff, regulation) used by government to achieve a policy objective
A musical instrument used at agricultural shows
A farmer's individual set of tools
The national anthem of Nigeria
questions.correct_answer: A specific tool or mechanism (e.g., subsidy, tariff, regulation) used by government to achieve a policy objective
questions.explanation: Policy instruments are the concrete means (subsidies, taxes, regulations, direct provision) by which policy objectives are pursued.

questions.question: Why do agricultural policies typically require periodic revision or review?
options: Because changing economic, environmental, and social conditions can make earlier policy assumptions outdated
Because the law requires new policies every single day
Because farmers are not allowed to comment on policy
Because agricultural science never changes
questions.correct_answer: Because changing economic, environmental, and social conditions can make earlier policy assumptions outdated
questions.explanation: Policies must adapt to evolving climate, market, population, and technological conditions to remain effective and relevant.
